newsitem.title: USA: Refiners fill needs with more expensive U.S. crude.
newsitem.headline: Refiners fill needs with more expensive U.S. crude.

text.p: Prices for U.S. cash crude grades increased Tuesday on refiner buying, tight foreign markets and favorable economics for filling needs at home.
Modest grade gains were overshadowed late in the session by a sharply bearish reaction to the weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) report.
API numbers blew out most expectations by posting a crude build of 6.94 million barrels for week ended May 9, and a similar 6.51 million barrel gasoline stock build.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing dropped around 25 cents to $21.00-$21.10 a barrel, retreating from regular NYMEX session losses that had pegged cash June WTI/Cushing at $21.30-40 a barrel.

Grades talked late at firmer differentials. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James last sold at premiums of 9 and 10 cents to benchmark June WTI/Cushing. LLS topped out at 13-14 cents over the marker, some 7 cents firmer than Monday.
Midland/WTI failed to excite traders, talked late at 33-30 cents under June WTI/Cushing.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire traded at 25, 33 and 35 cents under benchmark, steady to a shade firmer from Monday.
West Texas Sour/Midland also found favor with refiners looking to fill ratables, selling as firm as $1.33 under WTI, and talked late at minus $1.40-1.33.
Eugene Island barrels moved at a $1.45 discount, steady from Monday.
June WTI/Cushing Postings were widely talked around a $2.10 value, but fluctuating June/July rolls put postings to lofty levels above $2.15 earlier in the session.
June WTI/Cushing held a 4 cents edge over the July, giving back around 8 cents from Monday.
Traders said tight Brent markets and a lack of prompt foreigns aided sweet crudes in the Gulf. Production cuts in strife-torn Nigeria over the weekend also bolstered grades.
One cash dealer said continued supply concerns for Canadian grades underpinned WTS/Midland gains.
